channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Pope Leo to recite prayers in public Sunday, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will recite the Angelus prayer in public on Sunday, the Vatican Press Office said.

item.title: WATCH: Aboard USS George Washington as tensions rise in the Middle East
item.description: ABC News is aboard the USS George Washington near the Strait of Hormuz with rare front-line access as President Donald Trump weighs expanded operations against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

item.title: WATCH: New White House press secretary defends her record
item.description: President Donald Trump described new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia as an attorney, but Zacharia acknowledged that she took the bar exam and never passed.

item.title: Teen shooter kills 3 children, 1 teacher at elementary school in Bend, Oregon: Police
item.description: Police said they responded to a report of an active shooter at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon.

item.title: South African rugby player found dead in French hotel ahead of Champions Cup debut
item.description: A South African rugby player for the Lions team was found dead at a hotel in France Friday on the eve of a European Champions Cup game with ​La ‌Rochelle, local media reported. The player's identity has yet not been made public.

item.title: Crowds throng New Delhi and wave Indian flags amid escalating protests
item.description: Protests have intensified over a review of voter lists that critics say is politically motivated and threatens to disenfranchise voters. The Election Commission and Modi's administration deny these allegations.

item.title: Ethiopia announces interim government in Tigray, aims for polls in six months
item.description: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday announced the appointment of an interim administration to prepare elections in the northern Tigray region previously controlled by the Tigray People's Liberation Front that has clashed with government forces since September. The recent conflict revived a war that killed hundreds of thousands between 2020 and 2022.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates mass in hospital while recovering from lung cancer operation
item.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated a mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital Friday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, photos released by the Vatican showed. Doctors said his recovery was progressing normally but that further tests would show whether the cancer had spread.

item.title: 'America, with this president, is not our ally. Trump is a liar': French MEP Bernard Guetta
item.description: Our guest is veteran French journalist and commentator Bernard Guetta, who is a Member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group. He tells the programme that Donald Trump is "a liar, because he tried to tell the American people that Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance were responsible for the price of diesel. This is a pure lie. He (Trump) is responsible because he started the war with Iran." Guetta goes on to say that "without American intelligence sharing, Ukraine is weaker and weaker. That's terrible, to see the president of the United States giving a hand to Putin against Ukraine."

item.title: 'Thanks a lot, Trump': Wyoming conservatives divided ahead of US midterms
item.description: Famous for its cowboy culture, Wyoming is the least populated, the most rural and the most conservative of all the US states. With two weeks to go until the midterm elections, our reporters James André and Sylvain Rousseau travelled across this Republican stronghold and found that the party of US President Donald Trump is deeply divided in the Cowboy State.

item.title: Pope pictured for first time since cancer surgery as he leads mass from hospital
item.description: The Pope is said to be showing "continued improvement" as the first images of him were released following his lung cancer surgery.

item.title: Brewers sweep the Dodgers in the NLCS to reach first World Series since 1982
item.description: Garrett Mitchell hit a go-ahead homer in the sixth inning, leading the Milwaukee Brewers to a 6-4 comeback win over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series

item.title: EU and Canada seek closer ties: Will Canada become the EU's first associate member?
item.description: As the international context becomes more challenging for the European Union, the bloc is looking to boost its ties with like-minded allies. Canada is part of that architecture that the EU says it wants to build. The big news of EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's State of the Union speech in September was that Canada could become an associate member – an arrangement that does not exist for the EU's partners at the moment.

item.title: WATCH: Elon Musk unveils Tesla's new Roadster, and it can fly
item.description: Using SpaceX rocket technology, the sports car climbed a curved ramp and hurled itself to a controlled landing.

item.title: Drugs fuelling 'horrific' events seen in Waterford, says Irish justice minister
item.description: People who take illegal drugs are "supporting the horrific events we saw in Waterford", Irish justice minister Jim O'Callaghan has said.

item.title: Madeleine McCann prime suspect could face new rape trial
item.description: The prime suspect in the Madeleine McCann case could face a new rape trial after German prosecutors launched a legal bid to overturn his acquittal on a string of sex charges, unrelated to the missing British girl.

item.title: Spring-summer 2027 ready-to-wear collections: Africa in the spotlight at Paris Fashion Week
item.description: Fashion can absolutely be political, when it shapes identities and questions the balance of power. With his label Maxhosa Africa, South Africa's Laduma Ngxokolo is determined to put the continent in the spotlight. In Paris, Jacques Logoh, designer and founder of Togo's International Fashion Festival, gives African creatives a platform on the theme "Fashion against HIV". Plus Mossi Traoré stages his show at Paris's Père Lachaise Cemetery, to tackle the subject of death without taboo.

item.title: Iran live updates: Trump admin prepares options, including 'mother of all bombs'
item.description: A dozen people were killed Saturday during a "brutal" attack at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said.

item.title: Army chief says politicians to start 'frank conversation' with public to prepare for war
item.description: The head of the army says the UK's political leaders are about to start a "frank conversation" with the public about the need to prepare for war.

item.title: Pipe bomb 'pushed through letterbox' of home with mother and children inside
item.description: A pipe bomb exploded after being put through the letterbox of a Belfast home while a mother and her children were inside, police have said.

item.title: How books are being scanned and destroyed to train artificial intelligence
item.description: To train artificial intelligence models, millions of physical books are being digitised and destroyed. Our colleagues at France 2 investigate this controversial practice and the risk of seeing many rare second-hand books disappear forever.

item.title: Shooter kills teacher, three children at Oregon elementary school
item.description: A teenager shot and killed three children and a teacher on Thursday at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon, police said, adding the assailant was later killed by an armed bystander who pursued him into the building. Officers rushed to Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, a city of about 100,000 in the nation's northwest, after reports of a shooter on campus on Thursday afternoon. The three children who died on the scene were aged five, eight and 11, said Bend police chief Mike Krantz.

item.title: US considers hitting Iran with 'Mother of All Bombs'
item.description: The United States is considering using its biggest non-nuclear bomb against Iran if President Donald Trump should decide to renew combat in the war that has hit a deadlock, CNN reported Thursday. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, which erupted with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, have been at an impasse since the summer. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Zelensky rallies European allies as Trump ties slump
item.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky is seeking to rally European allies at a Brussels summit on Friday after saying Kyiv would no longer abide by US President Donald Trump's demands not to strike Russian oil refineries. Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.

item.title: EU leaders face budget divisions, discuss Ukraine at Brussels summit
item.description: European Union leaders gathered in Brussels on Thursday for a two-day summit to discuss the bloc’s next long-term budget, continued support for Ukraine and measures to strengthen Europe’s economic competitiveness amid rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty. They voiced strong opposition to a new proposal for the bloc’s long-term budget, raising serious doubt about whether the key spending package will be agreed by the end of year. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

item.title: How much money has Musk given to Republican groups since July? The quiz knows
item.description: Plus, this week saw comings and goings at the White House, the revenge of a child (reality) star, and Elon Musk doing Elon Musk things.

item.title: Nicolas Maduro and wife deny new torture charges as 'false accusations'
item.description: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro has rejected newly unsealed torture allegations against him and his wife as "false accusations".

item.title: France to witness a 'crossroads of anger' as mass protests expected on Saturday
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, October 16: French papers look ahead to Saturday's call for mass protests, which will bring together a number of social movements. Next, climate change has devastating consequences on communities in Afghanistan. Also, Libération publishes a special edition written in the style of Georges Perec. Finally, this year's animal of the year has been named.

item.title: No, this oil tanker didn’t carry Russian diesel to the United States
item.description: Following US President Donald Trump's October 9 announcement of an agreement signed with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel into the United States, a number of pro-Russian social media accounts began claiming that a Russian oil tanker was already carrying thousands of barrels of diesel to the United States. The ship was actually carrying fertiliser.

item.title: British man fined for causing death of his two-year-old son in Cyprus
item.description: A British father has been fined €3,000 (£2,500) for causing the death of his two-year-old son who fell from the fourth floor of a hotel in Cyprus.

item.title: Students join Yellow Vest protest: Greater collective strength versus risk of losing distinct voice
item.description: As student protests converge with broader public discontent over the rising cost of living in France, Genie Godula is joined by Sébastien Vieille, national secretary of the SNALC teachers’ union. He offers an assessment of a movement confronting political uncertainty, deteriorating school infrastructure and mounting fiscal constraints. Speaking from Montbéliard in eastern France, Vieille questions whether alliances with larger protest movements, including the Yellow Vests, will strengthen students’ demands or ultimately make them "less visible".

item.title: 'Fantasist' who murdered woman at Airbnb to exact 'brutal and fatal revenge' jailed
item.description: A "fantasist" who murdered a woman at an Airbnb to exact "brutal and fatal revenge" after she rejected him has been jailed for at least 28 years.

item.title: Indian authorities detain 'cockroach' movement founder Dipke ahead of new protest
item.description: Indian authorities on Friday detained Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the satirical youth movement "Cockroach Janta Party", ahead of a new protest in New Delhi, live images from the group showed. Police earlier closed a central New Delhi park in an attempt to stifle near-daily demonstrations calling for the election authority chief's resignation over the removal of more than 130 million people from voter lists.

item.title: Midterms 2026: Can Democrats capitalise on Latino voter regret?
item.description: In 2024, a 46 percent share of the Latino vote helped propel Donald Trump to the White House. But two years on, polls show that support has plummeted in spectacular fashion. Amid an immigration crackdown, violent ICE raids and the spiraling cost of living, some Latino voters say they regret having backed Trump at the ballot box. Now, as the midterms approach, can the Democrats capitalise on this sense of regret to win back what was once an essential part of their base? France 24 reporters Sam Ball and Barbara Gabel met with Latino voters and local Democrats in Phoenix, Arizona, to find out.

item.title: UK bookstores scramble as Sally Rooney's novels pulled over Palestine Action support
item.description: Critically acclaimed Irish novelist Sally Rooney's announcement that her books could no longer be sold in the UK due to her support for proscribed group Palestine Action has left British booksellers rushing to stock up on her works before distributors run out. The British government's ban on the group, which practiced non-violent direct action and sabotage against UK military assets believed to be working with the Israeli government, makes support for Palestine Action punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

item.title: Marseille's woes continue with second consecutive Europa League defeat
item.description: Things are going from bad to worse for Marseille. The French side suffered their second defeat in as many Europa League matches, losing 1-0 to Olympiakos. Lyon, meanwhile, are heading in the opposite direction, having secured a win over Premier League side Crystal Palace. Rennes, for their part, claimed their first Europa League victory of the season with a narrow 2-1 win over OFI Crete.

item.title: Live: Ukraine is ‘dependent’ on Starlink for intercepting Russian drones, Zelensky says
item.description: Ukraine depends on US satellite intelligence service Starlink to intercept jet-powered Russian drones, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said at an EU leaders summit in Brussels Friday. Kyiv was angered this week by disruptions to the critical satellite system hampering its military's ability to counter intense Russian bombardment ahead of the winter months. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: 9 former FBI agents who worked on Trump classified docs case sue over their firings
item.description: Nine former FBI agents who worked on President Trump's classified documents case have filed suit alleging that they were unlawfully fired over their role in the probe.

item.title: Minibus crashes into train at French Channel Tunnel entrance, injuring 19
item.description: Nineteen people were injured Thursday when a minibus carrying truck drivers crashed into a vehicle shuttle train at the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel near Calais, forcing a 90-minute suspension of shuttle services. Two people were hospitalised with serious but non-life-threatening injuries, French authorities said.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Rhode Island farmer sets new record for world's biggest pumpkin
item.description: David Muir reports on the new world record for heaviest pumpkin, which weighs 3,156 pounds – smashing the previous record of 2,856 pounds set merely a week ago.

item.title: France and Germany agree to ease EU car emissions rules in new deal
item.description: Paris and Berlin on Friday confirmed their deal aimed at protecting Europe's struggling automotive sector, having reached agreements on the flashpoint issues of EU car emissions and "made in Europe" components. A draft deal reviewed Thursday showed the two countries backing looser EU emissions rules for carmakers.

item.title: Children aged 5, 8 and 11 killed in US school shooting
item.description: Four people, including three children, have died after a school shooting in Oregon.

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks, Broncos face off in Thursday night NFL matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Omar Ruiz previews the Seahawks-Broncos showdown in Denver, including how Seattle’s top-ranked defense could challenge Bo Nix and whether Sam Darnold can bounce back after two interceptions.

item.title: Trump claims executive privilege to keep Kennedy Center conversations secret
item.description: A White House lawyer said Trump's executive privilege would also cover his conversations with advisers who don't serve in government.

item.title: WATCH: Rising number of young adults living with parents
item.description: ABC News’ Juju Chang reports on the growing trend of “boomerang kids” returning to live with their parents amid housing costs and financial concerns.

item.title: Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro pleads not guilty to torture
item.description: Ousted Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, each pleaded not guilty to new charges accusing them of torturing people to help them cling to power.

item.title: How Adam Hamilton plans on winning Kansas' Senate race
item.description: Can a Democrat flip the Kansas Senate seat for the first time in nearly a century?

item.title: 19 injured after Channel Tunnel collision between bus and train
item.description: Nineteen people have been injured after a collision between a bus and a train on the French side of the Channel Tunnel.

item.title: Wide majority of Americans oppose livestreaming Hasan execution: ABC/Post/Ipsos poll
item.description: A slim majority support the Fort Hood shooter's execution by firing squad.

item.title: WATCH: DIY Halloween costumes for this year’s viral trends
item.description: Lori Bergamotto shares easy, last-minute DIY Halloween costume ideas inspired by the people and pop culture moments that made headlines this year.

item.title: DOJ sues California over alleged non-citizens on voter rolls
item.description: LA County Clerk said they would refuse to access the thumb drive said to contain names of potential non-citizens believed to be on the state's voter registration list.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir hears from Georgia firefighters who helped deliver 15 puppies
item.description: Firefighters in Cobb County answered an emergency call to help a veterinary hospital deliver 15 puppies after a rescue dog came to the local animal hospital.

item.title: Norwegian teenage hitman who flew to UK to commit murder jailed
item.description: A Norwegian teenager who flew to the UK to carry out murder for an Iran-backed gang has been jailed for 20 years.

item.title: WATCH: Aggressive great white shark seen off Southern California coast
item.description: Experts say the shark could be hunting for seals.

item.title: School owner arrested after dozens of children killed in roof collapse
item.description: At least 34 children and a teacher have died after the roof of a private school collapsed in Pakistan.

item.title: WATCH: Measles, GLP-1s and anti-aging: How to protect your health
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi discusses the resurgence of measles, the potential health benefits of GLP-1 drugs and what we can do now to prevent disease and live longer.

item.title: WATCH: How to navigate rising prices this holiday season
item.description: ABC News’ Elizabeth Schulze reports on what to know about the latest inflation report and prices this coming holiday season.

item.title: WATCH: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ sends couple home on ‘Super Bowl Night’
item.description: ABC News’ Ginger Zee was behind the scenes as stars and their pro partners danced to songs performed during Super Bowl halftime shows through the years.

item.title: WATCH: SpaceX launch spawns "jellyfish" cloud in sky before sunrise
item.description: Families along the East Coast woke up to a majestic sight in the sky during SpaceX’s launch to the ISS.

item.title: WATCH: Viral museum worker gets unexpected honor
item.description: Alison Luchs has been working at the National Gallery of Art for almost 50 years, and almost a year into making art history videos with Gen-Z terminology, she was honored on the Time100 Art list.

item.title: Man and woman arrested after two adults and two children killed in house fire
item.description: Two people have been arrested over the deaths of two adults and two children in a suspected arson attack on a house in Ireland.
